summary.headline: Firstsource Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.6% YoY in constant currency to INR25.8bn; FY27 guidance is 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR25.8bn (US$283m), up 19.5% YoY in rupee terms and 11.6% in constant currency, with TeleMedik adding 1.3pp. EBIT margin was 12.2%, up 30bps QoQ and 100bps YoY, marking the sixth straight quarter of sequential expansion. Management said two timing effects (a delayed UK collections deal and paused Medicare Advantage payer ramps) hit Q4, which it views as deferrals rather than structural. FY26 revenue crossed US$1bn at INR95.6bn with 13.6% CC growth and 11.7% EBIT margin. Management framed the strategy as "Intelligence that operates" and guided FY27 CC growth of 10-13%.

segments.name: Banking & Financial Services (BFS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY and 5% QoQ in CC with six new logos. UK collections deal, delayed by regulatory approval, is now live; Q4 exit financial services pipeline described as among the strongest in recent quarters.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 16% YoY and 10% QoQ in CC with one new logo. Payer side saw short-term timing shifts as Medicare Advantage plans paused program ramps from January 2026; rates flat per management.

segments.name: Communications, Media & Technology (CMT)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3% YoY but fell 4% QoQ in Q4 due to timing of work packets and program transitions in large consumer tech engagements; management expects a return to healthier growth.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (retail, utilities)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% YoY but fell 8% QoQ in CC in Q4 on a seasonal retail dip after Q3 peak; four new logos added, and utilities demand described as steady.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% QoQ and 14% YoY in CC; management expects broad-based momentum to continue across the three core verticals.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% YoY and was flat QoQ in CC; two large deals won in Q4 and pipeline up about 60% over the last four quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guided at 10-13%; management said it has visibility to the lower end (10%) and expects the rest to come from pipeline and ramps.
FY27 EBIT margin guided at 12.25-12.75%, above the Q4 FY26 exit of 12.2%.
Management expects margin expansion of 50-75bps a year, with a longer-term target of 14-15% EBIT margin in the next couple of years.
Inorganic contribution to FY27 growth expected at about 2-2.5% from Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik.
Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters of FY27, not back-ended.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 20-22%.
Management said the two Q4 timing effects (UK collections and Medicare Advantage) are deferrals and should provide tailwinds in FY27.
capex_capacity: TeleMedik acquisition integrated in Q4; gives delivery presence in Puerto Rico, a US-compliant lower-cost location for healthcare and non-healthcare nearshoring.
Sales presence being set up in Canada; UK utilities and retail capabilities being replicated in the US; a North America utilities head was onboarded in the last three months.
Dedicated large-deal pursuit team set up; at least four large deals reported in each of the past five quarters.
Investment in go-to-market and technology continued through FY25 and FY26, with new roles including domain-plus-AI, forward-deployed engineers and builders.
Kairos described as the delivery platform for Intelligence that operates, designed to run in clients' own technology environments and model-agnostic across AI partners.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 added 11 new logos, including six strategic logos (potential of at least US$5m annual revenue each); FY26 added 47 new clients including 24 strategic.
FY26 had 150 clients above US$1m run-rate (up 34 over Q4 FY25); US$5m+ clients up 12 and US$10m+ clients up 2 in the year.
Top five and top 10 clients' revenue share fell 8% and 12% respectively over eight quarters.
Management said about 50% of strategic wins from the past eight quarters have converted into relationships above US$5m annual revenue.
Seven of the FY26 large deals came from new logos versus five in FY25.
Pricing for a US collections deal uses a platform fee plus per-interaction pricing with outcome accountability.
Management said AI is a structural TAM expander through scaffolding work, though clients' data quality and regulated processes slow full automation.
Offshore and nearshore delivery shift is accelerating in Europe; management said it may continue near term.
Management said FY26 organic growth was about 9.8-9.9% CC excluding Ascensos, Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik, versus about 12.1% ex-Pastdue and TeleMedik only.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Firstsource growing strongly when the market narrative says AI is cannibalising BPO revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani cited three drivers: TAM expansion as clients need AI scaffolding; share gains from challenger brands playing offense; and clients willing to move work away from in-house delivery with compelling commercial constructs.

qa_highlights.question: How should the rising debt (near INR1,600 crore) be viewed, and is there room for more acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Jain said 40-50% of cash flow goes to shareholders and the rest to acquisitions or growth; FY26 debt rose only about INR200m versus about INR700m in FY25, so the balance sheet leaves buffer for more acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 softer than expected, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani said Q4 was broadly in line barring two timing items: a UK collections deal delayed by regulatory approval into Q1 FY27 (now live), and Medicare Advantage payers pausing program ramps from January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic contribution in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik contributed about 1.5% to FY26 growth (organic about 12.1%). Inorganic contribution to FY27 is expected at about 2-2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the right to win against diversified IT services firms in the full-stack intelligent operations strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani argued that clients buy one continuous motion across implement, run and transform rather than pillars; Firstsource's size and domain depth in regulated workflows let it assemble teams around the customer problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much will investment in the Intelligence that operates strategy affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said efficiency saves from automation and offshoring fund new capabilities, and it remains confident of the FY27 margin guidance; FY26 margin expansion was about 74bps.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth phase across H1 and H2, and why does organic growth appear to slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters, not back-ended. Management said about 2% of FY27 growth is inorganic, and the lower end of guidance is backed by visibility plus pipeline and ramps.

risks_watch: Timing of the UK collections deal ramp (now live after regulatory delay into Q1 FY27) and resumption of paused Medicare Advantage payer programs; management said both are deferrals, so track Q1 FY27 healthcare payer and BFS revenue.

FY27 guidance of 10-13% CC requires about 2-3% QoQ CC growth; management has visibility only to the 10% low end, with the rest dependent on pipeline conversion and ramps, and about 2-2.5% of growth is inorganic.
Organic growth slowdown: FY26 organic was about 9.8-9.9% CC excluding Ascensos, Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik, versus about 12.1% ex-Pastdue and TeleMedik only; watch organic growth in FY27 quarters.
Margin: FY27 EBIT guided at 12.25-12.75% while investing in go-to-market, technology and new roles (domain-plus-AI, forward-deployed engineers); watch whether efficiency saves keep pace.
Balance sheet: net debt rose to INR16.3bn from INR13.2bn; management says 40-50% of cash flow goes to shareholders and the rest to acquisitions or growth, so further tuck-in M&A would add to debt.
CMT volatility (down 4% QoQ) and offshore/nearshore shift in Europe may persist near term; watch Europe and CMT sequential trends.
key_quotes: Q4 was broadly in line with our expectations at the start of the quarter with two exceptions, and I called that out in our opening comments itself.
But neither of this in our minds is structural.
what we don't expect this to be back-ended, but rather almost spread out across the four quarters itself, so you should see this evenly playing out.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the FY27 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin guidance, and on pipeline (above US$1bn, highest ever). It was more cautious on the near term, explaining Q4 softness as two timing effects and declining to comment on specific deal ramps, and it answered the organic-growth deceleration question with a qualified "about 9.8% to 9.9%".

adds.what: TeleMedik acquisition integrated in Q4, adding delivery presence in Puerto Rico (inorganic, already integrated)

growth.why: FY27 guided at 10-13% CC revenue growth (midpoint 11.5%) with visibility to the low end; backing is a >US$1bn deal pipeline (highest ever), 17 large deals in FY26 and about 2-2.5pp inorganic from Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik, but no new capacity is being added and the brief gives no specific contract numbers for the rest of the growth.
